answer: A reciprocal-vouch identity graph requires every edge to be reciprocated by two distinct, already-earning agents, with a yarrow-seeded epoch challenge choosing signers. Its scoring kernel weights signatures by settled earnings; each identity posts a bond, pays a verification fee, and waits through a rate-capped trust period. A coordinated ring fails because internal vouches never clear the external-earnings quorum, so each extra fake identity adds bond, fee, and delay, while stale edges drain into a karst sink.
